description.narrative: Kiribati, a Small Island Developing State (SIDS) in the Pacific, faces persistent structural challenges arising from its geographic dispersion, small domestic market, and remoteness from regional and global markets. These constraints limit productive capacity, increase the cost of doing business, and weaken trade competitiveness. In response, the Government of Kiribati has prioritized trade and private sector development as key drivers of inclusive growth and economic resilience, guided by the Kiribati 20-Year Vision (KV20) and operationalized through successive Kiribati Development Plans (KDPs) and the Trade Policy Framework (2017-2027).Within this national planning framework, the Enhanced Integrated Framework (EIF) has played a catalytic role in strengthening trade governance and institutional capacity. Building on achievements from earlier phases, EIF Phase III will be implemented through a nationally owned five-year Country Programme Document (CPD). To support this process, a consultant will be engaged to lead the preparation of the CPD, including conducting stakeholder consultations, assessing policy and institutional gaps, and drafting a results-based programme aligned with EIF priorities and Kiribatis national development objectives. The CPD will serve as the strategic roadmap for consolidating institutional gains and guiding targeted institutional strengthening and catalytic trade interventions under EIF Phase III.
